title: Honey Can Last for Thousands of Years
description: Archaeologists have found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that had not rotted. Here is why honey lasts.

scenes.text: Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs, thousands of years old, and it had not rotted.
Honey is mostly sugar with very little water. Bacteria trying to live in it get the water pulled right out of them.
It is also slightly acidic, and bees add an enzyme that helps produce a little hydrogen peroxide, which fights germs.
The trick is keeping it sealed. If honey soaks up moisture from the air, it can start to spoil.
Thank the bees for one of the longest lasting foods on Earth. Follow for more weird facts.
